reason: The text helper itself: it picks the font file of a weight (the one place a family is set)
The hidden bold copy that reserves a text's widest width, so selecting never moves the row: not a look
The hidden field that takes the typing of a code drawn in cells: invisible by function, not a design opacity
A sheet's list never covers the whole screen: it scrolls past 60 % of the window height
The smallest touch target (44 pt): a rule of the primitive, not a look (a smaller button grows its touch area)

The printed ticket's own font sizes for the Star, Epson and generic ESC/POS commands (printer units, one per platform). These three files are the original app's print path moved under src/printing without a change (commit 8bbf275 restored it); the sizes are the ticket's, not a screen's look, and the on-screen paper is themed apart (components.ticket_paper)

The on-screen paper's letters are the platform's fixed-pitch font (Menlo on iOS, monospace on Android): the printed ticket has a fixed pitch and the catalog's 10 fonts are proportional (docs/theme/tokens.md 2.5)
The canvas that draws a Star TSP100's ticket picture is a web view that must exist but not show: invisible by function, not a design opacity (as the OTP field's)
